newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Stadshypotek board says won't resign.
newsitem.headline: Stadshypotek board says won't resign.

text.p: The board of Swedish mortgage bank Stadshypotek, partly owned by the Swedish state, on Monday said it would not resign despite criticism by the Swedish government.
Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink earlier said he had no confidence in Stadshypotek's board following an announcement of a proposed merger with insurer Skandia.
Asbrink strongly criticised the plan and said the government's original plan to sell the state's 34 percent stake in Stadshypotek through a controlled auction remained valid.
But Stadshypotek chairman Gosta Renell told journalists at an analysts' meeting on Monday that the board would not resign.
"I don't want to comment about my position before I speak with Asbrink but it is the shareholders who decide on the board at a shareholders' meeting," Renell said.
"The board will be changed at a shareholders' meeting and not by a single shareholder. The board will stay until a shareholders' meeting."
Renell said the government's harsh criticism of the merger proposal was disappointing.
"It is surprising that the criticism is so hard and that they are not prepared to listen," he said.
